text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SEVODNYA
- The government will use its majority stake in Russia's Unified Energy System (UES) to exert stricter control over the inefficient monopoly.
- The government's inability to collect taxes keeps credit lines promised by Russia to CIS countries to zero.
- The government has adopted several documents supposed to overhaul inefficient power supplier UES radically.
- Trans World Group is planning to conquer Russia's soft drinks canning market.
- Russia is leading a consortium to build a $100 million power station in India.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Russia's natural monopolies have so far been able to get the upper hand in a fight against those who have tried to reform them.
- The rumoured nomination of First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov to head the ministry of fuel and energy could mean the end to the once powerful oil industry lobbyist in the government.
- St Petersburg governor Vladimir Yakovlev gives the go-ahead to a $500 million construction project to build a ringroad around the city, supposed to become part of the Moscow-Helsinki highway.
- Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov is seeking tax breaks, debt rescheduling, lower tariffs and a favourable import regime for Moscow enterprises.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russia's UES promises to lower tariffs for industrial users by 13 percent in 1997.
- The Russian Duma says it will monitor the situation with natural monopolies to protect them from possible raids by 'commercial structures'.
- Kazakhstan forms an oil giant Kazakhoil and says it plans to export oil to all destinations.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- The cabinet reshuffle is far from over and is likely to spill over to the second half of April.

Irkutsk and Novosibirsk regional governors, as well as a number of other top regional officials, have sent a letter to President Boris Yeltsin urging him to reinstate Purneftegaz as part of the oil-giant SIDANKO.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- The government and the state Pension Fund, under an order by President Yeltsin, have just three months left to pay all the overdue pensions.
- First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov puts all blame for huge debts crippling the energy sector on top UES managers.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
